title: Electrically controlled spin-splitting and asymmetric tunnel magnetoresistance in anti-altermagnets
abstract: Anti-altermagnets (AAMs) are a recently identified class of layered magnetic materials where opposite spin-splitting in adjacent layers creates a globally spin-degenerate band structure, rendering conventional spectroscopic detection highly difficult. In this paper, we theoretically demonstrate an all-electrical method to manipulate and probe this hidden magnetic order using a dual-gated transport junction. By applying a perpendicular displacement field, we break the spatial inversion symmetry of the lattice, explicitly lifting the global spin degeneracy. We attach ferromagnetic (FM) leads on either side of the AAM. Using quantum transport calculations, we show that this gate-induced spin-splitting manifests as a strongly asymmetric tunnel magnetoresistance (TMR) as a function of the lead magnetization. We identify specific crystallographic orientations where the TMR retains its symmetry despite the fully split bands, a direct consequence of exact momentum-space compensation. We further reveal that Rashba spin-orbit coupling guarantees robust, highly directional transport asymmetries even in the absence of an explicit chemical potential mismatch between the layers. Our findings establish a clear, electrically tunable framework for exploiting AAMs in next-generation spintronic architectures.
summary: This theoretical work proposes using a dual-gated junction to electrically probe the hidden magnetic order in Anti-altermagnets (AAMs). By applying an electric field, the system's spin degeneracy is lifted, causing a measurable, asymmetric tunnel magnetoresistance (TMR). The findings establish a tunable spintronic framework for exploiting these novel magnetic materials.
main_problem: To develop an all-electrical method to manipulate and probe the hidden magnetic order in Anti-altermagnets (AAMs), which possess a globally spin-degenerate band structure.
main_result: The study shows that applying an electric field breaks the spin degeneracy, leading to a strongly asymmetric tunnel magnetoresistance (TMR), while specific crystallographic orientations can restore symmetry due to momentum-space compensation.
method: Quantum transport calculations using the Landauer formalism applied to a tight-binding Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system is an Anti-altermagnet (AAM) sandwiched between two ferromagnetic (FM) leads, configured in a dual-gated transport junction. The magnetic order is characterized by opposite spin-splitting in adjacent layers.
key_observables: Tunnel Magnetoresistance (TMR) as a function of the lead magnetization ($b$) and the applied gate-induced displacement field ($\Delta\mu$).
important_parameters: Perpendicular displacement field ($\Delta\mu$), Rashba spin-orbit coupling ($\alpha$), and crystallographic orientation ($\phi$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the dual-gated FM-AAM-FM device architecture and the specific Hamiltonian terms governing the magnetic exchange and SOC.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic transport setup, TMR vs. Zeeman field showing asymmetry/symmetry dependence on angle, and momentum-space contours detailing the splitting and compensation effects.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the theoretical framework for probing AAMs via transport, demonstrating how gate-induced splitting causes TMR asymmetry, then analyzing the conditions (like specific angles or SOC strength) under which symmetry is maintained or enhanced.
why_interesting: The work connects magnetic order, symmetry breaking via electric fields, and transport signatures, which are core concepts in understanding emergent quantum phenomena in condensed matter systems.
